label: Schedule 1, paragraph 17 – meets requirements
text:
Date: 4 September 2025
Dear Sir/Madam
I understand that Lucy Williams wishes to access legal aid for a family dispute as a victim of domestic abuse. For this reason, I have been asked to provide a letter in accordance with regulation 33 and schedule 1 of the Civil Legal Aid (Procedure) Regulations 2012 (as amended).
I can confirm that our organisation is situated in England and Wales and has been operating for an uninterrupted period of six months or more.
I can confirm that we have provided Lucy Williams with support in relation to their needs as a victim, or person at risk, of domestic abuse.
In my reasonable professional judgement, Lucy Williams is a victim of domestic abuse.
The matters I have relied upon to support that judgement are:
• Lucy reported that Callum smashed household items during arguments, which was witnessed by their children.
• Lucy told me Callum would check her phone every day, read her messages and question her about who she had spoken to.
• Police attended the family home on 8 March 2025 following a 999 call and the incident was recorded as domestic abuse.
• Lucy has visible bruising on her arms that she told us was caused by Callum grabbing her.
• Lucy fled the home with the children and was referred to us by the local hospital.
• Lucy described Callum controlling all of the household money and giving her a small weekly allowance that she had to account for.
We have provided Lucy Williams with the following support: support attending court, risk assessment, help applying for emergency housing.
Lucy Williams needed this support because she fled the family home in fear for her safety and that of the children.
Yours sincerely,
Stuart Marsh
Domestic Abuse Support Worker
Netherford Refuge and Outreach
